newsitem.title: USA: US attache shaves Argentina wheat export forecast.
newsitem.headline: US attache shaves Argentina wheat export forecast.

text.p: A U.S. agricultural attache shaved his forecast for Argentina July-June wheat exports to 9.5 million tonnes from 10.5 million tonnes, citing higher prices and a slower-than-expected pace of purchases by Brazil.

In a report dated Jan 31 that was released in Washington this week, the attache, posted at the U.S. embassy in Buenos Aires, upped his corn production estimate to 14.5 million tonnes from 13.5 million tonnes.
Attache reports are not considered official USDA data.

"Conditions remain very favorable for corn, as moisture is generally widespread and evenly distributed over the main growing areas. In the northern areas of the corn production belt, silking and ear development are proceeding, with stands generally in good condition," the attache wrote.
In the World Supply and Demand Report released Jan 10, USDA pegged the Argentine corn crop at 13.5 million tonnes.
